questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify the expression using the properties of logical operations:

- First,  we use the distributive law (conjunction over disjunction):

$$
(A∧B)∨(A∧¬B)≡A∧(B∨¬B)
$$

- Next,  we use the fact that the disjunction of an expression and its negation is a tautology:

$$
A∧(B∨¬B)≡A∧\text{t}
$$

- Finally, we use the fact that the conjunction of an expression and a tautology gives the initial expression:

$$
A∧\text{t}≡A
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(A∧B)∨(A∧¬B)≡A.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify the expression using the properties of logical operations:

- First, we use the fact that the conjunction of a statement and its negation is a contradiction:

$$
¬[(¬X∨¬Y)∨(¬Y∧Y)]≡¬[(¬X∨¬Y)∨\text{c}]
$$

- Next, we use the fact that the disjunction of a statement and a contradiction equals the original statement:

$$
¬[(¬X∨¬Y)∨\text{c}]≡¬(¬X∨¬Y)
$$

- Then, we use a De Morgan's law:

$$
¬(¬X∨¬Y)≡¬¬(X∧Y)
$$

- Finally,  we simplify the double negation:

$$
¬¬(X∧Y)≡X∧Y
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
¬[(¬X∨¬Y)∨(¬Y∧Y)]≡X∧Y
$$

questions.problem: If $P$ is a statement, $\text{t}$ is a tautology, and $\text{c}$ is a contradiction, complete the following table of logical equivalences.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the following properties of tautologies and contradictions:

$$
\begin{aligned}A∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & A∧\text{t} & =A \\ A∨\text{c}=A\, &  & A∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{t}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{t} & =\text{t} \\ \text{t}∨\text{c}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{t} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{c}=\text{c}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{c} & =\text{c}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is shown below.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\text{t}∧\text{c}$ | $\text{c}$ |
| $\text{c}∨\text{c}$ | $\text{c}$ |
| $\text{c}∧¬P$ | $\text{c}$ |
| $P∨\text{c}$ | $P$ |
